# Results {#sec-results}

This chapter reports the results of the analysis planned in @sec-model (dated 2026-11-01): how does housing affordability — median gross rent relative to median household income — vary across the census tracts of Albany County, New York?

```{python}
#| warning: false
import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import spreg
from esda.moran import Moran

gdf = gpd.read_file("data/albany-analysis.gpkg")
gdf_valid = gdf.dropna(subset=["median_rent", "median_income"]).reset_index(drop=True)

n_tracts = len(gdf)
n_valid = len(gdf_valid)

from libpysal.weights import Queen
w_queen = Queen.from_dataframe(gdf_valid, use_index=False)
w_queen.transform = "r"

X = gdf_valid[["median_income"]].values
Y = gdf_valid[["median_rent"]].values

ols = spreg.OLS(Y, X, w=w_queen, name_y="median_rent", name_x=["median_income"], robust="white")
income_coef = ols.betas[1][0]
income_se = ols.std_err[1]
income_t = ols.tvals[1] if hasattr(ols, "tvals") else income_coef / income_se
r_squared = ols.r2

np.random.seed(42)
residual_moran = Moran(ols.u.flatten(), w_queen, permutations=999)

error_model = spreg.ML_Error(Y, X, w=w_queen, name_y="median_rent", name_x=["median_income"])
intercept_coef = error_model.betas[0][0]
intercept_se = error_model.std_err[0]
intercept_p = error_model.z_stat[0][1]
income_error_coef = error_model.betas[1][0]
income_error_se = error_model.std_err[1]
income_error_p = error_model.z_stat[1][1]
lambda_coef = error_model.betas[-1][0]
lambda_se = error_model.std_err[-1]
lambda_p = error_model.z_stat[-1][1]
```

## Main Finding

Across the `{python} n_valid` Albany County census tracts with both a rent and an income estimate (of `{python} n_tracts` total), median household income is a statistically significant predictor of median gross rent: each additional dollar of median household income is associated with an increase of `{python} f"{income_coef:.4f}"` dollars in median gross rent (White's robust standard error `{python} f"{income_se:.4f}"`, p `{python} "< 0.001" if ols.t_stat[1][1] < 0.001 else f"= {ols.t_stat[1][1]:.3f}"`), and income explains `{python} f"{r_squared:.1%}"` of the variation in rent across tracts (R²).

The OLS residuals themselves show significant positive spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = `{python} f"{residual_moran.I:.3f}"`, p = `{python} f"{residual_moran.p_sim:.3f}"`), meaning nearby tracts' unexplained rent is more similar than chance — a plain income-only model is missing a spatial pattern. A spatial error model confirms this: the spatial error term is itself significant (λ = `{python} f"{lambda_coef:.3f}"`, p = `{python} f"{lambda_p:.4f}"`).

## Results Table

| Variable | Coefficient | Std. Error | p-value |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| Intercept | `{python} f"{intercept_coef:.2f}"` | `{python} f"{intercept_se:.2f}"` | `{python} f"{intercept_p:.4f}"` |
| Median household income | `{python} f"{income_error_coef:.5f}"` | `{python} f"{income_error_se:.5f}"` | `{python} f"{income_error_p:.4f}"` |
| Spatial error term (λ) | `{python} f"{lambda_coef:.3f}"` | `{python} f"{lambda_se:.3f}"` | `{python} f"{lambda_p:.4f}"` |

: Spatial error model of median gross rent (US dollars per month) on median household income (US dollars per year), 82 Albany County census tracts. {#tbl-regression}

@tbl-regression reports the spatial error model's coefficients. The unit of the income coefficient is dollars of rent per dollar of income; the intercept and its standard error are in dollars of rent.

## Results Map

```{python}
#| label: fig-rent-map
#| fig-cap: "Median gross rent by census tract, Albany County, New York, 2024 (US dollars per month). Quantile classification, 5 classes. Tracts with no estimate (013706, 000800) shown in grey. EPSG:26918 (NAD83 / UTM zone 18N)."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib_scalebar.scalebar import ScaleBar

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 7))
gdf.plot(
    column="median_rent", scheme="quantiles", k=5, legend=True, ax=ax,
    missing_kwds={"color": "lightgrey", "label": "No estimate"},
    legend_kwds={"title": "Median gross rent\n($ per month)"},
)
ax.add_artist(ScaleBar(1, location="lower left"))
ax.axis("off")
plt.show()
```

@fig-rent-map shows the same pattern reported numerically above: tracts cluster, with higher-rent tracts concentrated toward the northeast of the county rather than scattered randomly, consistent with the significant positive spatial autocorrelation found in the Main Finding.

## Spatial Checks

```{python}
se_rent = gdf_valid["median_rent_moe"] / 1.645
cv_rent = se_rent / gdf_valid["median_rent"]
cv_mean = cv_rent.mean()
cv_max = cv_rent.max()
```

| Spatial pitfall | Status | Estimate |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Tracts do not represent individual households | Run | Not a numeric estimate — a scope statement: every finding above describes area-level patterns across `{python} n_valid` tracts, not individual households. |
| Margins of error on small-area estimates | Run | Coefficient of variation on rent averages `{python} f"{cv_mean:.1%}"`, ranging up to `{python} f"{cv_max:.1%}"` across tracts with an estimate. |

: Spatial checks promised in the proposal, with the estimate each one actually produced. {#tbl-checks}

## What Changed Since the Analysis Plan

The 2026-11-01 analysis plan is followed as written, with one addition made after seeing the first results: the Lagrange multiplier diagnostics for choosing between a spatial lag and spatial error model were not anticipated in the plan, since the plan did not commit in advance to one specification. **Added after the first results:** running both LM tests and using the robust versions to choose the spatial error model, once the diagnostics came back ambiguous rather than pointing cleanly to one model.

## Observation and Interpretation

Everything above is observation: what the data and the models show, stated in their own terms. What this might mean for housing policy in Albany — whether this income-rent relationship reflects discrimination, supply constraints, or something else, and what if anything should be done about it — is interpretation, and is deliberately kept out of this chapter. That discussion is drafted in `notes/2026-11-08-interpretation.md`, dated, to be developed in Progress Report 10 once Lecture 10 (discussion and conclusions) has been covered.
